Sen Kennedy to FB execs

The existence or nonexistence of the Christian god is irrelevant when we are discussing the cultural and ethical aspects of religion and their impact on societies.

Religions are a very useful cultural technology in that they are a vehicle for passing down useful cultural and ethical ideas. They are memeplexes composed of stories of people with virtues we want to emulate, vices we seek to eliminate, and parables that help us navigate complex social and judicial situations. They also help in keeping communities together: if everyone in a village believes that Freyja watches over their town in specific, that shared cultural belief can be used as a bridge when trying to resolve social issues (just as an example), and helps bind the cultural fabric that much tighter.

It is important to remember that people are, as a whole, somewhat dumb. This isn't intended as an attack on religion, with the whole "religion is for the dumb masses" angle - but I think it's easier for the less gifted to buy into a memeplex of cultural and ethical values when it's presented in the kind of packaged form that religion presents. Human brains are wired to understand stories, allegory, metaphor; this is almost assuredly why religions are entrenched in symbolism and that sort of thing.

Again, we're not interested in arguing the metaphysical aspects, here. We need a means of passing on useful and productive cultural and ethical values that work from one generation to the next, in ways that are durable and resistant to the passage of time. Religions serve that purpose very well: if they didn't, we wouldn't still have them (as they would have been replaced by something else in the memetic ecosystem). Whether or not a religion is "true" is less important than if the values it espouses produce moral citizens and successful societies.

We can't know what would have become of Europa if her people had remained Asatru. It's not worth looking into the yawning chasm of time to try to answer that question.
